name: cesium-sgp4-viewer
description: Show a whole satellite catalog on a CesiumJS globe, from a list of TLEs: every object at its SGP4 position, its orbit, its name, following the scene's clock.

paragraphs: Show a whole satellite catalog on a CesiumJS globe, from a list of TLEs: every object at its SGP4 position, its orbit, its name, following the scene's clock. SGP4 runs in web workers, and orbits are drawn by custom vertex and fragment shaders straight from GPU buffers, which keeps tens of thousands of objects smooth.
Live demo: a CelesTrak catalog snapshot (about 16,000 objects), in a vanilla TypeScript and a React version. Also runnable in Sandcastle, CesiumJS's online playground.

Plotting satellites from TLEs is a common need, and the straightforward way to do it in Cesium, one Entity with a SampledPositionProperty and a path per satellite, stops scaling after a few hundred objects: every entity is re-evaluated on every frame, every path re-sampled, and every label is one billboard per glyph. A public catalog has tens of thousands of objects.
features: SGP4 runs in web workers. The catalog is split across a small pool of workers (cores minus one, up to four). Each worker samples its satellites over a window of a few hours around the playhead and keeps its samples:…

The main thread only interpolates. A degree-5 Lagrange polynomial over 36 samples per revolution (more for eccentric orbits) stays close to SGP4: the unit tests bound the error at 50 m, a highly eccentric orbit included.
Points are one PointPrimitiveCollection, one draw call for the whole catalog, updated in place.

All orbits are one custom primitive. Rings are built once per hour of simulated time, uploaded to the GPU as they come out of the workers, and turned under the Earth by one matrix per frame. In 2D, the same buffers are…
Filters are free. Filtering by regime, name or anything else never propagates again: points are hidden, and the orbits' index buffer is rebuilt from per-satellite ranges.
